paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. Nehemiah has a finished wall, shut doors and guards on duty, and a city that is "large and spacious, but there were few people in it" (Nehemiah 7:4). A wall without people is just a very fancy fence. So God puts something into Nehemiah's heart (Nehemiah 7:5): it's time to count the people.

And look at what a list does: family lines get named, and the people of the towns get counted. I spent years in a drawer thinking nobody was keeping count of me, so this hits close to home. Your name matters to God too, and He keeps a better register than any drawer ever did. Even the priests who couldn't find their records were told to wait until a priest could consult the Urim and Thummim (Nehemiah 7:64-65).

So here's your takeaway, baker: building something is only half the job, because God cares about the people who get to live in it. The register of those who first returned ends with the priests, Levites and the rest of the Israelites settled in their own towns (Nehemiah 7:73), and that's the picture: a people with a place and a name. Show up, be counted and be part of the people of God. The story isn't over, either, so keep those ovens warm.
